headline: Riverlane and NVIDIA said that running the tuning of quantum error-correction software on a graphics chip cut a step from minutes to seconds.
score_reason: Company-reported technical benchmark, no outside review.
importance_line: Quantum researchers and hardware builders may get error correction that stays accurate as machines drift, though these are company benchmarks that outsiders have not reviewed.
summary: Quantum Computing Report reports that Riverlane, a quantum error-correction company, and chip maker NVIDIA announced benchmarks showing that an NVIDIA H100 graphics processor cut the training time for recalibrating a decoder from minutes to seconds. The decoder is the software that spots and fixes qubit errors, and the recalibrated settings reduced logical errors by several percent up to a factor of two, according to the announcement.
notes: Companies' own figures as relayed by QCR.
